source: proposal §5 channel vocabulary v1 (2026-09-14); project-owned names, no vendor names. v2 (ADR-0002 amendment 2026-09-30): the gaze is a target point per frame (`gaze`); gaze_yaw / gaze_pitch are readouts in defined degrees

gaze.frame: the socket's local frame (default_head_rest.obj, the envelope of ADR-0002 D1), metres
gaze.rule: every head turns each of its OWN eyes so that eye's line of sight passes through target_m; vergence and parallax follow from the head's own eye positions. Between frames a head interpolates each eye's rotation, not the point. A head whose eyes cannot turn that far clamps and reports gaze_clamped per frame, never silently. A head without 3D eyes maps the point through its own eye positions in this frame: the rule is where the eyes look, not how they are drawn

sources.LOOK_AT: the master's rig carries an animated look-at object (conventions scene_naming.eyes.look_at): its position per frame
sources.CAMERA: the state map names CAMERA for the window: the camera's position — eye contact
sources.NAMED_TARGET: the state map names an object for the window and the default head's gaze ray meets it: the hit point
sources.FAR: none of the above: the point on the default head's gaze ray at far_m — two eyes parallel within 0.16° each

gaze.migration_rule: the slice's shots were authored with the yaw/pitch pair and record no distance: the gaze ray runs from the midpoint between the default head's eyes along their shared direction (NAMED_TARGET where it meets the window's named object, else FAR). Measured 2026-09-30 (slice/measurements/gaze_vergence_2026-09-30): SHOT_001 1023-1027 converge on the ball at 0.26 m; every other frame of the three shots stays within 0.16° per eye of what was rendered
gaze.readout_rule: gaze_yaw / gaze_pitch drive no head since v2: they are the default head's gaze direction toward target_m — yaw the azimuth about the socket's up axis (+ = the character's left), pitch the elevation — in channel units of readout_degrees per 1.0, for QC and state detection (check_states). The exporter asserts that the default head's rig obeys these degrees within readout_tolerance_deg
gaze.readout_tolerance_status: PROVISIONAL — the slice's rig drives the eyes by exactly these degrees (build_character.py GAZE_YAW_DEG / GAZE_PITCH_DEG); a rig with a non-linear eye mapping fails it and the vocabulary's degrees are re-measured, never the rig re-fitted silently

sides: _l / _r are the character's ANATOMICAL left and right (socket +X = anatomical left)
control_convention: placeholder rig: one float custom property per channel on the FACE_CTRL empty, already in channel units. A real rig maps its own controls here: input_range → output_range, linear.

combination_rules.effective: lid closure = max(max(0, -lid_aperture), blink); lid widening = max(0, lid_aperture) * (1 - blink)
combination_rules.meaning: blink closes the eye on top of the held lid pose and never beyond full closure: lid_aperture -1 is already closed, so a blink adds nothing there; a blink on a widened eye (fear) closes it fully, so the widening fades as the blink rises. Every consumer of the performance track (the default head's rig, every head technology) applies this rule to the raw channel values
combination_rules.status: clarification of vocabulary v1 ('blink: on top of lid_aperture'), not a new channel meaning — contractor Q19/Q21, 2026-09-17
combination_rules.why: two independent closure targets summed to 2.0 at lid_aperture -1 with blink 1 and drove the lid through the eye; a widening target left a gap under a full blink
